text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. The main idea is that developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Each time they do this, automated builds start automatically. These builds compile the code and check that everything works correctly. As part of the same process, the system also runs tests to make sure new changes do not break existing features. This helps teams catch issues early, when they are easier and cheaper to fix. Many companies use CI pipelines, which are a series of automated steps that build, test, and sometimes deploy the software. In short, CI saves time and improves code quality.
